note: THE GESTURE IS IN, AND THE DEMONSTRATION IT EXISTS FOR HAS RUN. Implementation: `ann gate! <id> confirm --review` runs the SAME `runGateReview` the `submit!` door and the frame call, against a submission already standing — a second CALLER, never a second path. The four refusals (review-not-confirm · review-takes-no-decision · review-no-submission · review-with-flag) are decided before anything is spent, so a refused gesture costs no model call and writes nothing; accept/rework/human are reported through ONE shared rendering so the two doors cannot drift, and the ABSENCE is deliberately NOT shared — a submission degrades visibly to the human, an explicit `--review` fails by name (the operator's Q2 answer: FAIL). CLI-only by construction, and this is the part the first draft got wrong: making `gate!` async turned the route OFF for EVERY gate write, because `resolveDispatch` refuses a Promise by name (not-exposed). The handler is therefore SYNC, and `--review` is the only branch that returns a Promise — which is exactly what keeps it off the served surface. The route also refuses any field whose value is a `--`-prefixed token, so `{decision:"--review"}` is a 400 rather than a review and `{feedback:"--force"}` is a 400 rather than an override.
